_meta.indication: NUBEQA is indicated for the treatment of patients with non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC).

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; darolutamide 600 mg twice daily vs placebo, all patients on a GnRH analog or bilateral orchiectomy.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with high-risk non-metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (nmCRPC) with a PSA doubling time ≤ 10 months.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was metastasis-free survival (MFS) by blinded independent central review.
pivotal_trials.result: Median MFS 40.4 months (darolutamide) vs 18.4 months (placebo); HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.34, 0.50); p<0.0001.

key_safety: The most common adverse reactions (≥2%) were fatigue (16% vs 11% placebo), pain in extremity (6% vs 3%), and rash (3% vs 1%). Common lab abnormalities included decreased neutrophil count (20% vs 9%) and increased AST (23% vs 14%). Seizure incidence was 0.2% in both arms.
target_moa: Darolutamide is a nonsteroidal androgen receptor (AR) antagonist that competitively inhibits androgen binding, AR nuclear translocation, and AR-mediated transcription.

rems.type: No REMS is needed; safe use can be managed through accurate labeling and routine pharmacovigilance.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Division did not refer this application to an advisory committee because darolutamide is not the first drug in its class, the safety profile is acceptable, and the clinical trial design is similar to previously approved products in the class.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Priority review.

summary.text: Darolutamide received regular (traditional) approval under Priority review, based on the pivotal phase 3 ARAMIS trial; it had received Fast Track designation for nmCRPC in 2016. Approval was not based on accelerated approval, and no advisory committee was convened.

citations.quote: The basis of the recommendation for regular approval of darolutamide is a favorable benefit-risk profile in ARAMIS (NCT02200614), a multinational, randomized, double-blind, phase 3 trial of the anti-androgen darolutamide compared with placebo in patients with high-risk nmCRPC conducted under SPA agreement with FDA.
